architecture_summary.operational_context: cloud-hosted microservices architecture with API gateway, message queue for async communication, and per-service databases

threat_actors.name: external_attacker
threat_actors.motivation: financial gain through payment data theft and order manipulation
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: exploit public-facing API gateway vulnerability or credential stuffing
non_capabilities: no physical access to cloud infrastructure
no zero-day exploits for underlying cloud platform
no insider knowledge of internal service topology

threat_actors.name: malicious_insider
threat_actors.motivation: data exfiltration for competitive advantage or sabotage
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: legitimate access to internal network via compromised developer workstation or CI/CD pipeline
non_capabilities: no direct access to production database credentials (stored in vault)
no ability to modify API gateway configuration
no access to payment service encryption keys
no physical access to cloud provider facilities

threat_actors.name: opportunistic_botnet
threat_actors.motivation: automated credential stuffing and vulnerability scanning for any exploitable service
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: credential stuffing against API gateway auth endpoints or scanning for known CVEs in exposed services
non_capabilities: no ability to chain multiple exploits
no persistence mechanisms beyond initial access
no capability to bypass WAF rules

attack_paths.impact: initial foothold in DMZ, potential bypass of authentication
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: API gateway is internet-exposed; known CVEs in gateway software (e.g., Kong, NGINX, AWS API Gateway) are regularly exploited

attack_paths.impact: authenticated access as legitimate user, bypassing initial access controls
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: credential stuffing and phishing are prevalent; API gateway auth endpoints are high-value targets

attack_paths.entry_point: compromised API gateway -> internal service-to-service call
attack_paths.impact: persistent access to user service, ability to read/modify user data
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: if initial access gained, lateral movement to internal services is feasible; web shells common in compromised web apps

attack_paths.impact: exfiltration of payment card data, PII, transaction history
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: payment database is high-value target; if payment service compromised, direct DB access likely

attack_paths.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Command and Control Channel
attack_paths.impact: data exfiltration via message queue to external listener, bypassing direct DB access controls
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: requires compromise of order_service first; message queue may have egress filtering

attack_paths.impact: inventory corruption, financial loss through incorrect stock levels, order fulfillment failures
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: message queue is trusted internal channel; injection possible if order/payment service compromised

attack_paths.entry_point: compromised developer workstation -> internal network access
attack_paths.impact: lateral movement to order service using stolen service account credentials
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: insider threat with network access; service-to-service auth often uses shared secrets or certificates vulnerable to theft

attack_paths.entry_point: CI/CD pipeline compromise -> access to infrastructure-as-code repositories
attack_paths.impact: database credentials extracted from config files, direct database access
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: credentials often stored in config files or environment variables in repos; CI/CD compromise is realistic

mitigations.control_name: Identities and credentials are issued, managed, verified, revoked, and audited for authorized devices, users, and processes
Vulnerability management plan is developed and implemented
Manage Access Control for Remote Assets
Configuration change control processes are in place
Utilize an Automated Tool to Inventory Network Devices

findings.severity_rationale: API gateway is internet-exposed; credential stuffing (T1078) has high likelihood and leads to authenticated access bypassing perimeter controls
Known vulnerabilities in API gateway software (T1190) provide initial access vector; patching cadence may leave window of exposure
Web shell persistence (T1505.003) on user service enables long-term access to user data; logging coverage is partial
Payment database (T1213) contains cardholder data; direct exfiltration would trigger PCI-DSS breach notification and severe financial/reputational impact
Message queue exfiltration (T1041) is lower likelihood due to egress controls but would bypass database access monitoring
Inventory data manipulation (T1565.001) via message queue injection causes direct financial loss and operational disruption; message queue is trusted channel
Insider lateral movement via Pass the Hash (T1021.004) is high likelihood given internal network access; service-to-service auth uses shared secrets
Database credentials in configuration files (T1552.001) accessible via CI/CD compromise; vault adoption is incomplete
